clue.text: Down-to earth types aren't prone to be this

definitions.text: Down-to earth types aren't prone to be this

parts.words: Down-to earth types aren't prone to be this
parts.note: people lying down on the earth who are not face-down must be lying on their backs

explanation.surface: A remark that practical, grounded people are never lazy or passive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-to-earth' suggests sensible people, and 'prone' suggests 'inclined to'; read literally, those lying on the ground but not face-down are lying face-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, the opposite posture to prone; it also means passive.

clue.text: The make-up of perms, causing some flutters

definitions.text: The make-up of perms, causing some flutters

parts.words: The make-up of perms, causing some flutters
parts.note: pretends to be about hairdressing; really a football-pools permutation is built out of extra wagers

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the ingredients of hair perms making people nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perms' looks like hairdressing; it is a permutation on the football pools (a British betting game), made of extra wagers, and 'flutters' is British slang for small bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Side bets are extra wagers placed alongside a main bet; a flutter is a small gamble.

clue.text: Foreshadow the last of the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Finishing the wine is a sign of things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to be a sign or warning of something to come.

clue.text: Are you a member of this establishment, Sir ? Sounds like it

definitions.text: Are you a member of this establishment, Sir ? Sounds like it

parts.words: Are you a member of this establishment, Sir ? Sounds like it
parts.note: a titled man addressed as Sir would belong to a club for such men, whose name is said the same as a late-night venue

explanation.surface: A doorman asks a gentleman whether he belongs to the club.
explanation.walkthrough: A man called Sir is a knight, and a club for knights sounds the same as a late-opening venue for dancing and drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is an establishment open late for dancing and drinking, with members.

clue.text: Writer implies the North's warmer

indicators.note: the answer's letters, split up, state something that implies what the following words say

parts.note: S (south) followed by a word for colder says the south is cooler, from which it follows the north is the warmer

explanation.surface: An author hints that the northern part of the country is the warmer one.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the German poet's name after the S: 'S chiller', the south is colder, which implies the North is warmer. Friedrich Schiller wrote Ode to Joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and playwright, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Said to produce a catty smile ?

definitions.text: Said to produce a catty smile ?

parts.words: Said to produce a catty smile ?
parts.note: the cat in Alice in Wonderland famous for grinning, plus the word photographers ask people to say to make them smile

explanation.surface: A spiteful remark that makes someone smirk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cheshire Cat grins in Alice in Wonderland, and people say 'cheese' to smile for a photo; the answer is also a crumbly English county cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire cheese is a crumbly English cheese; saying cheese makes a smile, and the Cheshire Cat grins.

clue.text: African forces endlessly up to mischief

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, so it has no end

parts.note: impish means playfully mischievous

explanation.surface: Troops in Africa are causing trouble without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Impis were Zulu regiments of warriors, so armed forces in southern Africa.

clue.text: From which one descends for a time below 25

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed below another comes after it

parts.note: the answer to 25 across is the line round the Earth's middle, giving the word line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone climbs down after waiting a while under clue 25.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is EQUATOR, often called 'the Line'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineage is a line of ancestors, from whom a person is descended.

clue.text: Careers as viewed by film-directors

definitions.meaning: careers as a verb means dashes headlong
the first unedited prints of a day's shooting, which directors watch

explanation.surface: Professions as seen by people who make films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like a noun (jobs) but is a verb: to career is to race along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash wildly, and the day's unedited film prints are the dailies screened for directors.

clue.text: His assassination as dramatic as its setting

definitions.text: His assassination as dramatic as its setting

parts.words: His assassination as dramatic as its setting
parts.note: a leader shot while watching a play in a theatre, so the killing happened in a dramatic setting

explanation.surface: A murder as theatrical as the place where it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The American president was shot in 1865 at Ford's Theatre in Washington, during a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth US president was assassinated in Ford's Theatre while watching a comedy.

clue.text: After inflation's dealt with, easy to control

definitions.text: After inflation's dealt with, easy to control

parts.words: After inflation's dealt with, easy to control
parts.note: an airship that has been filled with gas can be steered; the clue pretends to be about economics

explanation.surface: Once rising prices are tamed, the economy becomes manageable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' wants to be economic; it is the filling of a gas bag, and the word for steerable is also the noun for an airship.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigible means steerable, and as a noun it names a steerable airship that must be filled with gas.

clue.text: Mildred's flowers ?

parts.note: the name Mildred split as 'mild red' describes a pale red colour, and that colour word is also a garden flower

explanation.surface: Asking which blooms belong to a woman called Mildred.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Mildred as MILD RED: a mild red is a pale rose colour, and the same word in the plural names a family of garden flowers (dianthus).
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are clove-scented garden flowers of the dianthus family, and pink is a light, mild red.

clue.text: Drink for complaint ?

parts.note: a hot meat broth served to an invalid with a complaint; also a word for a grumble joined to a word for a brew

explanation.surface: Asking what to drink when one is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is both an illness, for which this broth was the classic restorative, and a grumble (BEEF) to which a brew (TEA) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a broth made from stewed beef, traditionally given to invalids.

clue.text: Address theatre in Behan's titi role

parts.note: 'Ho!' is a call used to address or hail someone
the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: Speaking to a theatre about a part in a play by Brendan Behan.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan Behan's play is The Hostage; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The captive held in Brendan Behan's play gives the drama its name, so this is the title part.

clue.text: Back pound — notice it going up and down periodically

indicators.note: placed at the front, it tells the solver to read the whole string of pieces from end to start

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
an ad is a notice in a paper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money and a public notice rise and fall in value at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the whole string L + AD + IT, giving the letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides rise and fall at regular intervals, so tidal describes something going up and down periodically.

clue.text: Strange war-cries may cause flight

indicators.note: the letters of the war-cries are put in a strange, new order

explanation.surface: Unfamiliar battle shouts can make soldiers flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' wants to mean running away; it is flying, which a propeller makes possible.
explanation.definitionFit: An airscrew is an aircraft propeller, the thing that drives a plane into flight.

clue.text: Norman, the schoolboy's champion ?

parts.note: William of Normandy won England in 1066; a schoolboy's winning horse chestnut on a string bears the same name

explanation.surface: Asking which boy named Norman is the school's champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like a first name; it is William, the Norman who took England. Schoolboys play conkers (a British game smashing horse chestnuts on strings), and a winning conker is a conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror was the Norman duke who invaded England; a victorious conker is also so called.

clue.text: Uriah, putting on airs, turned into a hypocrite

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming, falsely humble clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Dickens's creep, acting superior, became a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah gives HEEP (Uriah Heep of David Copperfield); 'putting on' joins AIRS, and 'turned into' rearranges HEEPAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharisees were a Jewish sect whom the Gospels condemn as self-righteous, so the word means a sanctimonious fraud.

clue.text: Abstractly representing "limbs-coy composition

indicators.note: a composition is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An artist's abstract piece shows bashful arms and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for an idea through a sign rather than by direct depiction.

clue.text: Main place of execution for police department?

parts.note: the Yard is short for Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters
an arm is a branch or department of an organisation

explanation.surface: Asking where the police section carries out hangings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the high sea; sailors were hanged from the end of a ship's spar. Scotland Yard is London's Metropolitan Police HQ.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers at sea were hanged from the end of a ship's yard, the spar on a mast.

clue.text: Fraction revealed by division, in theory

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part of a whole emerges from theoretical arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninth is one of nine equal parts, a common fraction.

clue.text: Seen to be excluded from freeze

parts.note: being excluded from something means not being part of it
iced means frozen, so freeze points to the past form

explanation.surface: Being spotted while left out in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noticed has been observed, so seen and noticed are synonyms.

clue.text: Cecil's wonderful island

definitions.meaning: Cecil ..., the British imperialist after whom Rhodesia was named
the Greek island whose Colossus was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world

explanation.surface: A man named Cecil owns a marvellous island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonderful' is literal: the Colossus of this island was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Rhodes was the British colonialist; the Greek island bore the Colossus, an ancient Wonder.

clue.text: As far as TV viewers can see ?

definitions.text: As far as TV viewers can see ?

parts.words: As far as TV viewers can see ?
parts.note: the line where earth meets sky marks the limit of sight, and the BBC science series of that name is what television audiences watch

explanation.surface: Asking how much television audiences can make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The limit of anyone's sight is a line in the distance; Horizon is also a long-running BBC science documentary series, hence 'TV viewers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible limit where land seems to meet sky is as far as anyone can see; it is also a BBC series.

clue.text: Like the belt for which many a lightweight comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals, a large number
an is the form of a before a vowel
oz, an ounce, is a light weight

explanation.surface: A boxer's championship belt that many small fighters win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' wants to be a boxing class; it is OZ, an ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonal means relating to a zone, a belt or band of territory.

clue.text: Cross it to see how the other half lives

definitions.text: Cross it to see how the other half lives

parts.words: Cross it to see how the other half lives
parts.note: the phrase about the other half usually means the rich; here it is the other hemisphere of the globe

explanation.surface: Advice to step over a social line and see how wealthier people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other half' normally means a different social class; here it is the other hemisphere, reached by crossing the line round the middle of the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary line around the Earth's middle divides it into northern and southern hemispheres.

clue.text: As one end of compass needle is, northward ? Just the reverse

definitions.text: As one end of compass needle is

indicators.note: a word for northward, abbreviated, must be read backwards

parts.note: N-WARD is a short way of writing northward, N standing for north

explanation.surface: Describing how a compass needle points north.
explanation.walkthrough: One end of a compass needle is pulled (drawn) north; write northward as N-WARD and 'Just the reverse' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism pulls one tip of a compass needle towards the pole, so that tip is attracted, or pulled.

clue.text: Fouls can make us cross, — but team leader intervenes

indicators.note: the first letter of the team comes between other letters of the rearranged words
the letters of the following words can be made into something new by rearranging them
a team's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: Foul play angers fans, but the captain steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fouls' looks like a noun for infringements; it is a verb meaning blocks. 'can make' signals the mix, 'leader' the team's first letter, and 'intervenes' puts it inside; 'us' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To foul a line or passage is to block it, so fouls is a synonym of blocks.

clue.text: Pudding appears in no meals : I cooked

indicators.note: cooking food changes it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A dessert is present in none of the meals I prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is a wheat grain cooked with milk as a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Game needs number of cards shuffled to make 10

indicators.note: cards shuffled are mixed, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 10 across is the word for an airship
a pack holds 52 cards, LII in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A card game requires shuffling a set number of cards to reach ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Add LII (52, the cards in a pack) to the answer and 'shuffled' rearranges the lot into the 10-across answer, DIRIGIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.
